slides.heading: What is a set?
slides.body: A set is a well-defined collection of objects. We write A = {1, 2, 3}. Elements are members of the set.

slides.heading: Roster vs set-builder
slides.body: Roster: list elements. Set-builder: {x | x is even, x < 10}. Both name the same idea in different forms.

slides.heading: Union & intersection
slides.body: A ∪ B = elements in A or B or both. A ∩ B = elements in both. Draw two circles (Venn) to see it.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: A = {a,b}, B = {b,c,d}. Find A ∪ B and A ∩ B. Answer: ∪ = {a,b,c,d}, ∩ = {b}.

slides.heading: Relation vs function
slides.body: A function assigns each input exactly one output. Vertical line test: a vertical line may hit the graph only once.

slides.heading: Domain & range
slides.body: Domain = allowed inputs. Range = actual outputs. Example: f(x)=√x has domain x ≥ 0.

slides.heading: Function notation
slides.body: f(x) = 2x + 1 means input x, output 2x+1. f(3) = 7.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.body: f(x)=x²−1. Find f(2) and f(−2). Both give 3 because (−2)²=4.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: g(x)=3x−4. Find g(0) and g(2). Answers: −4 and 2.

slides.heading: Slope meaning
slides.body: Slope m = rise/run = (y2−y1)/(x2−x1). Positive slope goes up to the right.

slides.heading: Slope-intercept form
slides.body: y = mx + b. m = slope, b = y-intercept (where the line hits the y-axis).

slides.heading: Parallel & perpendicular
slides.body: Parallel lines: same m. Perpendicular: m1·m2 = −1 (for non-vertical lines).

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: What is the slope of y=−3x+7? Answer: −3.

slides.heading: Standard form
slides.body: y = ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0. Graph is a parabola.

slides.heading: Vertex idea
slides.body: Vertex x-coordinate = −b/(2a). Opens up if a>0, down if a<0.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.body: y = x² − 4x + 3. Vertex x = 4/2 = 2, y = −1. Vertex (2,−1).

slides.heading: Roots
slides.body: Solutions of ax²+bx+c=0. Factor or use the quadratic formula.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Does y = −x² + 1 open upward or downward? Answer: downward (a=−1).

slides.heading: Logarithm idea
slides.body: log_b a = c means b^c = a. Log undoes exponentiation.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Evaluate 3^0 and 5^(−1). Answers: 1 and 1/5.

decks.subject: MATH
decks.title: Right Angled Triangle and Trigonometric Ratios

slides.heading: SOH-CAH-TOA
slides.body: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.

slides.heading: Right triangle
slides.body: One angle is 90°. Pythagoras: a² + b² = c² for legs a,b and hypotenuse c.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.body: Legs 3 and 4 → hypotenuse 5. sin of the angle opposite 3 is 3/5.

slides.heading: Special angles
slides.body: Remember 30°–60°–90° and 45°–45°–90° side ratios.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: In a 3-4-5 triangle, cos of the angle adjacent to 4 is 4/5.

slides.heading: Percent change
slides.body: Increase = (new−old)/old × 100%.

slides.heading: Simple interest
slides.body: I = PRT (principal × rate × time) when rate is a yearly decimal.

slides.heading: Profit & loss
slides.body: Profit = SP − CP when SP>CP. Loss when CP>SP.

slides.heading: Degree & terms
slides.body: Polynomial: sum of terms a_n x^n. Degree = highest power with nonzero coefficient.

slides.heading: Add/subtract
slides.body: Combine like terms only (same power of x).

slides.heading: Multiply
slides.body: Distribute: (x+1)(x+2)=x²+3x+2.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.body: (2x²+3)+(x²−5)=3x²−2. Degree 2.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Degree of 7x³ − x + 1 is 3.
